page.example: A self-managing page: header actions, search, table and pagination wired to the demo backend, with create and edit in a modal form. The Available tab is a view: the same list with a filter of its own, searchable too. The headers sort the list and the columns menu hides the category or the price. The Owner column names who each product belongs to, and the filters panel offers to filter by owner once the products have two owners or more. The Organization column and its filter show only while the products you see belong to two organizations or more, as a superadmin's do.

move.label: Move to...
move.tooltip: Move the selected rows to another folder

folders.example: With categories the page browses folders, and the last node of the breadcrumb counts what the folder holds, folders apart from products, across every page. A folder shared with someone, or inside one that is, shows the shared folder icon. Leaving for a route under the page and coming back keeps the folder, the search, the page and the selection. Drag a product, or the selected rows, onto a folder to move them there; the Move to... action does the same from the keyboard. Where rows have owners, both offer only the folders of the owner of the rows, and a selection of several owners cannot move. The headers sort the list on the backend.

sharing.example: With isSharedEnabled the page adds a Shared with me tab, after the main tab and its views, listing the folders others shared with you; the breadcrumb starts at the shared folder, so the folders of its owner above it never show. Select one of your folders and open the menu to share it: the form lists who can view it and who can edit it, and searches the people and groups of the organization. A document offers View next to its name, a standard action with an action of its own that opens what the name opens. Select your folders and documents and open the menu to change their owner: the form names the current owner and searches the active users of the organization, and BeyPageTransferConfig sets the line that explains what the new owner gets. This example answers from a backend of its own.
